replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: I don't get anxious about math itself, but I do worry when it feels too abstract or disconnected from real life. My neuroticism score of 65 makes me sensitive to stress, so I focus on concrete examples to keep it grounded.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: I used AI tools like chatbots to solve puzzles and check answers. It helped me understand concepts step by step, but I preferred hands-on practice over automated solutions. I found it useful for quick checks but not for deep learning.
replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write the equation in standard form: ax² + bx + c = 0. Then calculate the discriminant (b² - 4ac). If positive, two real solutions; zero, one solution; negative, complex solutions. Use the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(discriminant)] / (2a).

To find stationary points, take the first derivative f'(x), set it equal to zero, and solve for x. Then plug those x-values back into f(x) to get the y-coordinates. These points could be maxima, minima, or points of inflection.
